```{r Problem 1}
library(tidyverse)
library(moderndive)

#import and quickly view the data
data("early_january_weather")  
skimr::skim(early_january_weather)

#There are 15 variables in this data set

#find the variable names 
names(early_january_weather)
#The names of the variables are  "origin"     "year"       "month"      "day"        "hour"       "temp"       "dewp"       "humid" "wind_dir"   "wind_speed"    "wind_gust"  "precip"     "pressure"   "visib"      "time_hour". For year we can see that it is 2013 for every entry and that temp is in Fahrenheit.

#find number of rows and columns
nrow(early_january_weather) #358 rows
ncol(early_january_weather) #15 columns

#mean temperature
mean(early_january_weather$temp, na.rm = TRUE) #mean temp is 39.58 Fahrenheit.

#Create scatterplot
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(early_january_weather,
            aes(x = hour, y = temp, color = humid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Temperature over Time (colored by Humidity)",
       x = "Time (hourly)", 
       y = "Temperature (°F)",
       color = "Humidity") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma") +
  theme_minimal()

p

#The scatter plot of temperature (temp) versus hour of day (time_hour), shows a daily cycle. Temps are lowest in the early morning hours and rise through the day, peaking in the afternoon before cooling again at night. Humidity values (shown by color) are higher during cooler nighttime hours (purple/blue points) and lower during warmer daytime hours (yellow/orange points).

#save plot 
ggsave(
  filename = "scatter_temp_time.pdf",  # name of the file
  plot = p,                            # the ggplot object
  width = 8, height = 4, units = "in", # size of the PDF
  device = "pdf"                       # file type
)
```
